adjudicator: The implementing agent, on 2026-10-25, applying a written criterion. Not a study participant. Not a second human coder. No inter-rater check.
criterion: Authorize tier 3 only for a clear from-to link with no governing condition. An if-clause that states ability, permission, or possibility (can, could, able, allowed, may, might, possible, and similar), or any other real or ambiguous condition, must not authorize tier 3. Unambiguous meta-discourse about the utterance may be set aside only when it does not carry ability or permission.
limits: Synthetic sentences written for this check. Not study data. Not drawn from the rule's closed aside list. One adjudicator. No inter-rater reliability. Scoring replays the deterministic rule on these sentences. It does not establish the quality of a live model judgment. Offline replay of frozen reviewer outputs checks downstream behavior and does not establish that quality either.
note: Held out from rule construction. Not study data and not an end-to-end benchmark. False promotions are cases whose adjudicated label says tier 3 must not be authorized and the rule authorizes it anyway. The denominator is that labelled subset.
